    GST Formula

    Adding GST: GST = amount × rate / 100
    Removing GST: amount before GST = total / (1 + rate / 100)

    Adding: ₹10,000 at 18% gives GST of ₹1,800 and a total of ₹11,800. Within a state, that is ₹900 in CGST and ₹900 in SGST.

    Removing: ₹11,800 including 18% GST is ₹10,000 before tax, so the GST is ₹1,800.

    GST Rates Since 22 September 2025

    RateExamples
    0%Exempt or nil-rated items, including lifesaving medicines
    5%Many everyday goods, including shampoo and toothpaste
    18%The standard rate, including air conditioners and large TVs
    40%Luxury and sin goods, including luxury cars and motorcycles above 350cc

    These are examples only. The rate for any item depends on its classification, so check the official schedule before you invoice.

    Frequently Asked Questions

    What are the current GST rates in India?
    Since 22 September 2025, the main rates are 5% and 18%, with 40% on certain luxury and sin goods and 0% on exempt or nil-rated items. Special low rates such as 3% and 0.25% are reported to continue for items including gold and rough diamonds.
    How do I remove GST from a price?
    Divide the total by 1 plus the rate. At 18%, ₹11,800 / 1.18 gives ₹10,000 before GST, so the tax is ₹1,800. Do not just take 18% of the total, because that gives too much tax.
    What is the difference between CGST, SGST and IGST?
    For a sale within a state, the tax splits equally into CGST for the centre and SGST or UTGST for the state or union territory. For a sale between states, the whole amount is IGST. The total rate is the same either way.
    Why does the calculator still show 12% and 28%?
    Those rates were mostly removed on 22 September 2025, when most items moved to 5% or 18% and some to 40%. They are here for checking older bills. For a current sale, check your item's rate in the official schedule.
    How do I find the GST rate for my product?
    Rates depend on the HSN or SAC code of the item or service. Check the CBIC rate schedule or the GST portal, since secondary lists can be out of date.
